message.content: {"name": "reject_trade", "parameters": {"public_message": "No. St. James is not for sale at any price in this structure. Cash was the only offer, and that door is closed for now.", "private_thought": "Reject. Giving St. James hands p1 2/3 orange (with Tennessee) plus ~$341, one NY landing from the best set. Connecticut is only useful as a light-blue package for Ventnor, and that second trade is not locked. Cash cap was $250; they refused. Stop chasing. Keep St. James and Park Place as blockers. Never complete dark blue for p2."}}
message.reasoning:
I am evaluating a trade offer to decide whether to accept, reject, or counter.

I am weighing the trade against p1's assets. I have four properties and $705 cash. p1 has three railroads and a stranded light blue set. p2 has pink utilities and Boardwalk.

p3 owns Baltic, Vermont, States, Illinois, Ventnor, and Pennsylvania Avenue. They have two of three light blue properties. I hold Park Place, which blocks their dark blue set.

I am considering trading St. James Place for Connecticut Avenue to complete my yellow monopoly with Ventnor. I am also noting that p3 holds the veto on the yellow set.

I have decided to reject the trade. St. James Place is an orange property, and p1 already holds Tennessee and Kentucky. That would give them a complete orange monopoly plus cash. I will not sell St. James Place to p1.

I am weighing a counter-offer. I could raise the cash offer above $250. Another option is trading Oriental Avenue for Connecticut, which would swap light blue pieces instead of giving St. James Place to p1.

I cannot trade Oriental Avenue for Connecticut because that would prevent me from completing the light blue set with p3. I also ruled out Park Place and my yellow properties as counter-offers, since giving either would destroy my strategic position.

I am now considering a counter-offer that pairs higher cash with a smaller property. I want to avoid giving St. James Place to p1, since they specifically need that orange piece to complete their monopoly.

I will reject the trade. I have no railroads to offer in return. A final cash counter would waste a turn and signal desperation.

I am reconsidering a counter that pairs St. James Place with cash and a railroad. I am calculating whether p1 would have enough money to purchase New York Avenue, which is unowned.

Orange properties have the highest landing probability and lowest house cost in Monopoly. Completing my yellow set while giving p1 a path to orange is a net loss. I will reject the trade.

I am rechecking the property colors. I realized Baltic Avenue is brown, not light blue. The light blue set is Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut. This confirms that trading Oriental for Connecticut would complete my light blue set.

I have two of three yellow properties. p1 holds one orange piece and has no orange monopoly yet. Red is evenly split across all three players, so no one can complete it. p2 already owns two of three pink properties.

I will trade Connecticut to p1, then swap Oriental and Connecticut with p3 for Ventnor. This completes my yellow set while giving p3 the light blue monopoly.

p3 previously rejected a $200 offer plus Oriental Avenue for Ventnor because they need a completed monopoly. This confirms the two-step plan is viable if I can acquire Connecticut cheaply.

p1 is pricing Connecticut as the key to my yellow set and demanding St. James Place plus $100 in return.

I am now calculating that p1 would have roughly $341 after receiving St. James Place. That would allow them to purchase New York Avenue, which is unowned and only $200. An orange monopoly with houses is the strongest set in the game.

I will reject the trade. I cannot guarantee p3 will trade Ventnor for the light blue set, and an orange monopoly would outclass my yellow set. A higher cash counter would waste a turn without fixing that risk.

I am drafting a firm but non-hostile public message to keep future negotiation options open. I also briefly reconsidered accepting the trade, which would leave me with $605 and the yellow set.

I am now calculating the financial impact of accepting the trade. After receiving Connecticut, I would have roughly $605 and three houses on my yellow properties. That is about $1350 in house value, which I cannot afford to build out.

With $605, I could build a modest yellow set with four houses. p1 would immediately purchase New York Avenue and build three houses on orange. Orange properties hit more often than yellow, so that set would be devastating.

I rejected the idea of offering Park Place to p1. That would let p2 buy it and complete their dark blue set, which would bankrupt other players.

I calculated that paying $350 for Connecticut would leave me with only $355 after the swap. That is enough for just two houses on my yellow set, which would be too weak to justify the cost.

I checked the yellow property rent schedule. Two houses on one property yields roughly $360 to $390. That is too weak to justify the cost and the light blue chips. p1 will not accept cash. I will keep the Connecticut offer capped at $250.
